Row.name: C-APPROVE-TIME-REVIEW
Row.Charter: Teach `ngrace review --change` as a step **before** `ngrace gate approve`, at both the spec and the plan stage: `ngrace-spec` approve step, `ngrace-plan` rule 15, and `ngrace-reviewer` broadened from one moment ("before judgment") to three. **Must ship the partial-review caveat, corrected by [F150.1](#f150.1)**: at **spec** approve the scope and WriteEvidence audits report `not-run` (no plan on disk) while the attempt-pair audit *runs* and reports `ran over 0 fail→pass pair(s)` — a clean line over an empty denominator, which is a **weaker** signal than `not-run` and reads as substantiation. Quote each audit's actual status string per stage; a grouping phrase is how [F147](#f147)'s manufactured-pass shape gets taught. Named here 2026-09-03 by [F149](#f149), **amended by [F150](#f150)**: the bundle must also ship what a clean approve-time review looks like, because at **plan** approve the scope audit reports the bundle's own `spec.xml` and `plan.xml` as out-of-scope writes on every bundle (`decisions.md` only when it changed *after* the recorded base — [F150.2](#f150.2)), and the `WriteEvidence` audit reports a third status there, `unable-to-determine`, distinct from its spec-stage `not-run` (at **spec** approve it does not run at all, and naming those findings as expected there teaches a not-run audit as if it had spoken — [F150.1](#f150.1)) — an instruction that produces unexplained errors on first use is a trap, not guidance. **Also carries [F152](#f152)**: show the closed approval lexicon whenever approval is requested, one approval request per message naming one artifact, and record the ratifying phrase verbatim — three concerns in this bundle now (approve-time review, F150's expected-findings guidance, F152's lexicon rules), plus the carried XML-escaping item, and its Intent must say so rather than let scope accrete. Searched before minting: `C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT` made the gate the status writer, `C-APPROVAL-SCOPE` covers the phrase and the close acts ([D19](#d19)/[D20](#d20)), `C-REVIEW-SURFACE` created the detector surface; **none says when review runs.**

Row.name: C-PAYMENT-RECORD
Row.Charter: **Charter.** Make already-discharged findings retirable by recording their payments in a form the derivation can read. A finding retires when its `PaidBy` names an archived bundle, and `PaidBy` is derived from registry rows and a phrase in archived specs — so a payment nobody recorded is a payment that never happened, as far as the ratchet is concerned. - **Direct historical rows in `registry.xml`**, ruled by the maintainer. Archived specs are never edited, so the row is the only route. - **The row must be visible to the derivation.** `kind` is a closed union (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:69`) and the payer derivation filters to `chartered` (`:731`); `collectPaidBy` additionally requires `StatusText` matching `/delivered|superseded/i`. A new `kind` is inert unless the union and filter widen. - **Every payment is verified, never asserted.** Each row carries the symbol, test name, or `file:line` that discharges the finding. Recording a payment that did not happen would convert eligibility — the enforcement itself — into a formality, which is [D28.1](#d28.1)'s defect in a worse form than a config key. - **Scope for margin, not the minimum.** The window after a move is `252 + Δ_retired` against a staged wrap that grows every session.
Row.Pays: [F187](#f187) in part, and whichever live findings the audit verifies as discharged.

Row.name: C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW
Row.Charter: **Charter.** Make retirement create room instead of erasing its own. The ceiling is re-derived as `base + headroom` at every move, so retiring content removes an equal amount of ceiling and the staged entries can never be flushed ([F183](#f183)). - **The window formula.** `Base_k = Base_live − Δ_retired` and `Ceiling_k = min(Ceiling_(k−1), Base_live + H)` at one `--retire` event, where `Base_live` is the **pre-move** footprint. Retirement then opens a window of `Δ_retired + H` that the next pass closes. The `min` is required, not optional: without it the ceiling rises whenever growth outpaced the previous retirement. - **Findings genre only.** Rulings, registry and index keep their current timing, each with a stated reason. The rulings `CodifiedIn` tagging pass is a separate bundle. - **`H` stays a constant derived in tracked repository space** — never a function of the staged buffer or any untracked state. A ceiling read from `.ngrace/scratch/` would be unreproducible from a fresh clone and greenable by appending to a `.gitignore`d file, which is [D28.1](#d28.1)'s rejected shape in a worse form than a config key. - **Remove the spent one-time exception**, whose clearing premise was false ([F186](#f186)), and move the provenance of the 1883 ceiling to a constant a validator asserts rather than a comment that drifts from the number.

Row.name: C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY
Row.Charter: **Charter.** Ship the **ongoing** retirement operation and the first codification tagging, so the record can retire as fast as it grows. - **A `PaidBy` feed.** Something must write `<PaidBy>` onto a live finding when the bundle that paid it archives. Today `collectPaidBy` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:372-410`) derives the map correctly but runs **only** in the one-shot `--split` path. - **Detection that reads the derivation, not just the stored element**, *and* a derivation wide enough to fire. The validator exits 0, and so would a re-derivation: the shipped `collectPaidBy` returns **0** live-eligible ([F180](#f180)). Widening it is a spec decision to argue against `D28.1`, not a refinement to assume. - **A retirement move.** A command that moves an eligible entry to its retired sibling and re-derives the live root's `base` / `ceiling`. There is no such command; `--split` refuses once `decisions.md` is a stub. - **First `CodifiedIn` / `TaughtIn` tagging**, with both resolution checks already shipped. [D27.1](#d27.1) is the first candidate by its own text. [D24](#d24) against `C-REWORK-CIRCUIT` remains *a candidate to verify, not a fact to restate* ([D28.1](#d28.1), [F123](#f123)). - **Headroom sizing is an open question, not a given.** [F181](#f181) measured headroom derived from median **entry size** while the pressure comes from **arrival rate**. Re-deriving a ceiling after legitimate retirement is not the same act as raising a number to pass, but the spec must say which it is doing and answer [D28.1](#d28.1)'s *"a budget that can be raised to pass is not a budget"*.

Row.name: C-CODIFY-DECISIONS
Row.Charter: **Chartered 2026-09-07 by the maintainer**, verbatim: *"option C"*, on four itemized variants. The position is deferred **deliberately, and the deferral is the point**: a position decision costs the decisions genre roughly forty lines, while a charter row costs it nothing — staged charter rows are not `[FD]\d` entries and so are not counted in the decisions wrap at all. Ratify a position once this bundle has made room. Priority needs no stating in the meantime: this is the only chartered work that can open the rulings window, so nothing else can sensibly precede it. **Charter.** Give the decisions genre a working retirement trigger. **It is not, as this row first read, the thing blocking the flush** — that claim was a measurement artifact, corrected the same day in [F191](#f191): both genres fit their windows today. What remains true is that **a live resolving `CodifiedIn` is `decision-eligible-still-live`**. That is the validator invariant, not a census of the live set. A resolving `TaughtIn` annotates and does not retire. The retired sibling is the precedent that a move is possible; it is not a population figure. - **Codification alone may not be enough, and the spec must prove which.** [`C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW`](#named-bundle-registry) applied its window formula to the **findings genre only**; the rulings call site still clamps against the post-move base. Whether a decisions-genre retirement opens the window, leaves it unchanged, or shrinks it is a question to derive from the code and confirm on a fixture — not to assume from the findings behaviour. - **The evidence standard is the load-bearing question.** [D28.1](#d28.1) retires a decision when its prose invariant is *permanently replaced by an automated machine check* that enforces it *unconditionally*. A tag on a decision merely **related** to a shipped test retires live governance text on a false premise, and retirement is one-way in practice. [D24](#d24)'s tag was gated on two **named tests passing at execution**, which is the pattern. - **`TaughtIn` versus `CodifiedIn` is unresolved.** Teaching a rule in skill prose is not enforcement, so a spec that uses the tag without settling what it means is deciding by accident. - **The bundle must pay for itself.** Whatever chartering and closing costs the decisions genre, the scope must retire more, with margin — every staged figure on this work has aged in the same direction.
Row.Pays: the decisions half of [F187](#f187), and whichever live decisions the audit verifies as codified.
